The head of Iran’s Supreme National Security Council said that the waterway will remain closed until the United States met certain conditions.

![Boats on a hazy, still sea, with brown cliffs just visible in the distance.](https://static01.nyt.com/images/2026/08/08/multimedia/08int-iran-mwcl/08int-iran-mwcl-articleLarge.jpg?quality=75&auto=webp&disable=upscale)

# Iran front heats up as US faces mounting pressure, Israel confronts a growing dilemma - analysis

## As tensions with Iran rise on Monday, the US faces the prospect of military escalation in the Gulf, while Israel confronts Hezbollah attacks in Lebanon and keeps Gaza a secondary front.

[Follow us on **Google**](https://www.google.com/preferences/source?q=https://www.jpost.com/)

US forces operating in the Strait of Hormuz, July 17, 2026.

(photo credit: Screenshot/X/@PeteHegseth)

ByMAJ.-GEN. (RES.) GIORA EILAND

The Iranian front appeared to be heating up as of last week, with the United States seeking to break Iran's blockade of the Strait of Hormuz and Tehran responding with missile fire against the United Arab Emirates and Oman.

The US tried to achieve two things that Iran did not want, and could not, accept. The first was to [ease Iranian pressure](https://www.jpost.com/middle-east/article-904891) in the Strait of Hormuz. There was a good chance Iran would have agreed to this if its concession had been met with an American concession, namely lifting the US blockade on Iranian oil exports. ![People gesture beneath an Iranian national flag as they take part in a procession.](/wp-content/uploads/2026/08/AFP__20260804__C3WL3EA__v1__HighRes__IranReligionIslamShiaArbaeen-1785973213.jpg?resize=730%2C410&quality=80)

Video Duration 01 minutes 57 seconds 01:57

Iran Tightens Strait of Hormuz Control as US Blockade Disrupts Global Shipping

[![](/wp-content/uploads/2019/05/83990b95560343dd90352efbb62bb090_6.jpeg?resize=96%2C96&quality=80)](/author/maziar_motamedi_190127060358086)

By [Maziar Motamedi](/author/maziar_motamedi_190127060358086)

Published On 8 Aug 20268 Aug 2026

**Tehran, Iran –** Iran’s authorities are weighing a finalised arrangement with Oman over the Strait of Hormuz, but top officials maintain that the strategic waterway’s [full reopening](/news/2026/8/7/trump-says-war-cant-go-much-longer-whats-the-latest-on) will hinge on concessions from the United States.

Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi on Saturday said the agreement with Oman was “very close”, but cautioned that a full reopening of the strait would depend on the US staying true to commitments given as part of a June memorandum of understanding (MoU) that were violated.

# Ukraine's grain exports could fall by 53% after russian attacks on ports - media

![Grain exports from Ukraine may decrease by 53% due to russian attacks on ports. Photo: UkrAgroConsult.](https://ukranews.com/upload/media/2026/08/08/6a76e9bd22fbf-ukr-wheat3_913.jpg.webp "Grain exports from Ukraine may decrease by 53% due to russian attacks on ports. Photo: UkrAgroConsult.")
![Google Preferred](/images/icons/social/google_preferred.webp)

Ukraine's agricultural exports could be cut by more than half this season after russian attacks disrupted the operation of Black Sea ports.

This was reported by [Bloomberg](https://www.bloomberg.com/news/articles/2026-08-07/ukraine-grain-exports-to-slump-after-russian-strikes-on-odesa).

According to the Ministry of Agriculture of Ukraine, the country could export about 29.6 million tons of agricultural products in the 2026-27 marketing year, which is 54% less than the previous estimate of 64.4 million tons.

Wheat exports could fall by 53% to 8.3 million tons compared to the previous forecast.

Ukraine is one of the world's largest grain suppliers, with the agricultural sector generating more than half of the country's export revenues last year.

# Another crack in the China-U.S. truce

### Beijing announced new countermeasures against Washington while warning that further U.S. restrictions could provoke a stronger response

[PC](https://substack.com/@whatshappeninginchina)

∙ Paid

**Welcome back to What’s Happening in China,** your weekly China brief.

The Chinese government on Wednesday announced a series of countermeasures against the U.S. in response to recent actions by Washington, including tightened controls on drone exports to the U.S., as well as key components and related technologies, on a “case-by-case basis.”
